questions.stem:
Can artificial intelligence (AI) truly capture human consciousness? Louisa Hall’s novel Speak pursues this inquiry by weaving together five stories across different centuries, from a Puritan woman’s diary to an AI’s confessions. These narratives reveal unexpected connections, suggesting that our drive to preserve human expression through technology stems from fear that without such mediation, our voices might be lost to time. Hall ultimately posits that AI represents not merely a technological achievement but the latest manifestation of an existential attempt to transcend mortality.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.A: It begins with a question about the role of AI in society, explains how an author seeks to answer that question in a novel, and proposes that preserving human expression is more important than technological advancement.
options.B: It introduces a novel’s central question, describes how the author employs a specific narrative structure to investigate that question, and presents the author’s conclusion about a broader human concern.
options.C: It presents a provocative paradox, summarizes how a novel questions the assumptions underlying the paradox, and reframes the author’s message as an argument about AI and human mortality.
options.D: It poses a philosophical dilemma, outlines five storylines that explore this dilemma across different time periods, and reveals how these stories converge to challenge conventional views about technology.

questions.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• 2024: Spain and Portugal sponsored a workshop to address recent encounters between Iberian orcas and marine vessels off the Iberian Peninsula.
• Many of the 637 documented incidents involved pods of orcas damaging vessels by ramming, nudging, or biting the rudders.
• Studies of Iberian orcas suggest recent increases in tuna populations have reduced the time the orcas spend hunting by 99%.
• Researchers believe this shift has increased the number of interactions between marine vessels and understimulated orcas.
• The workshop advised mariners to avoid orcas pending further testing of the efficacy of TAST, a harmless acoustic deterrent.

The student wants to make and support a claim about Iberian orca behavior. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: The recent destructive behavior of Iberian orcas may be the result of understimulation, given that orcas' interactions with marine vessels have increased as the orcas have spent less time hunting.
options.B: Tuna populations have increased by approximately 99% off the Iberian Peninsula due to changes in the hunting behavior of Iberian orcas.
options.C: As supported by the workshop's analysis of 637 encounters between vessels and Iberian orcas, TAST is a harmless and effective acoustic deterrent.
options.D: In 2024, Spain and Portugal sponsored a workshop that addressed incidents where pods of Iberian orcas were ramming, nudging, or biting the rudders of vessels.

Defensive Behavior and Reproductive Traits of Select Bird Species $$\begin{array}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \text{Scientific name} & \text{Common name} & \text{Broken-wing display?} & \text{Incubation (days)} & \text{Incubation duty} & \text{Max broods per year} \\ \hline \text{Bucephala islandica} & \text{Barrow's goldeneye} & \text{No} & 34 & \text{1 parent} & 1 \\ \hline \text{Haematopus bachmani} & \text{black oystercatcher} & \text{No} & 33 & \text{2 parents} & 1 \\ \hline \text{Zenaida macroura} & \text{mourning dove} & \text{Yes} & 15 & \text{2 parents} & 7 \\ \hline \text{Poocectes gramineus} & \text{vesper sparrow} & \text{Yes} & 13 & \text{1 parent} & 3 \\ \hline\end{array}$$ In an extensive review of existing literature, Léna de Framond and team cataloged the prevalence of broken-wing display—a defensive behavior observed in Charadrius semipalmatus (semipalmated plover) and many other species—throughout the Aves class. Documentation of the display in 285 species across 52 families suggests the behavior likely evolved independently multiple times, prompting the team to consider ecological and life-history characteristics with hypothesized associations to the behavior's emergence, including traits related to reproduction investment and future reproduction potential. Based on their review of those traits, the team concluded that __________

Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to complete the conclusion?

options.A: among species with more than one parental incubator, the use of broken-wing display is associated with greater incubation duration.
options.B: broken-wing display is most often observed in species with less opportunity to reproduce in a year due to longer incubation periods.
options.C: incubation duration and capacity for multiple broods are more strongly associated with the use of broken-wing display than the number of parental incubators is.

questions.stem:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

The Antikythera mechanism is an ancient Greek hand-powered mechanical device discovered in a shipwreck in 1901. Constructed around the late 2nd or early 1st century BCE, it is widely regarded as the world's oldest known analogue computer. It used a complex differential gear train comprising over thirty bronze gears to predict astronomical positions and eclipses. It tracked the Saros cycle (a 223-lunar-month eclipse prediction cycle) and the Metonic calendar cycle. It also included an indicator display showing the four-year cycle of the ancient Panhellenic athletic games (including the Olympic Games).

The student wants to emphasize the sophistication of the Antikythera mechanism's design. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

options.A: The Antikythera mechanism, an ancient Greek device recovered from a shipwreck in 1901, was hand-powered.
options.B: Regarded as the world's oldest known analogue computer, the Antikythera mechanism employed a differential gear train of over thirty bronze gears to predict astronomical positions and eclipses while tracking both the 223-lunar-month Saros cycle and the Metonic calendar cycle.
options.C: The Antikythera mechanism was constructed around the late 2nd or early 1st century BCE.
options.D: An indicator display on the Antikythera mechanism showed the four-year cycle of the ancient Panhellenic athletic games, including the Olympic Games.

Text 2

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the hypothesis discussed in Text 1?

In the world's democracies, proportionally few elected representatives are young adults. While some philosophers argue that certain types of underrepresentation (of women, for example) are unfair in principle and should be remediated via quotas, there is broad agreement that youth underrepresentation is not inherently unfair since it is universal (all people are underrepresented when young), temporary (underrepresented young people become overrepresented older people), and reflective of a legitimate concern (lack of relevant experience). Accordingly, when philosopher Juliana Uhuru Bidadanure advocates for youth quotas for elected representatives, she does so on the basis of their instrumental value for promoting youth interests, arguing that __________

Which choice most logically completes the text?

options.A: young adults may lack certain kinds of experience but those experiences are not relevant to the question of whether youth underrepresentation is fair in principle.
options.B: age-related quotas would alleviate the inherently unfair overrepresentation of older people that tends to occur in the world's democracies.
options.C: youth underrepresentation may be fair in principle but leads to worse outcomes for young adults than could be achieved with more proportionate youth representation.
options.D: it does not matter that youth underrepresentation is universal, temporary, and reflective of a legitimate concern since it is inherently unfair.

questions.stem:
A 2025 study performed by Simon Townsend and colleagues presents evidence that bonobos, close relatives of chimpanzees, are capable of a rudimentary compositionality in communication —that is, they can organize sounds they make such that the order carries meaning in addition to the sounds themselves. After reviewing bonobo calls recorded in forests of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Townsend's team claimed that bonobos sometimes paired calls in specific orders and that the contexts of such pairs indicate they were deliberate communications rather than products of chance. The team based their claim on mathematical analysis of how frequently particular call pairings occurred and the situations in which they were used.

Which finding, if true, would best support the researchers' claim?

options.A: A bonobo grunt seems to function as a request for other bonobos to join in whatever activity is ongoing, since bonobos emitting a grunt did so during potentially collaborative contexts such as feeding, nesting, and grooming.
options.B: Bonobos used a single yelp or a single peep as an imperative, but a yelp appeared to be closer to a command, while a peep tended to function as a suggestion.
options.C: While a single whistle from a bonobo was often an attempt to organize groups, a whistle preceded by a peep sound usually occurred in the presence of a charged social situation.
options.D: When bonobos paired grunts with other calls, they did not appear to alter the meaning of the grunt, suggesting that call combinations in bonobos function as simple repetition rather than as compositional sequences.

questions.stem:
Text 1 is from George Eliot’s 1860 novel The Mill on the Floss. Text 2 is from Rabindranath Tagore’s 1921 nonfiction book Glimpses of Bengal.

Text 1
The wood I walk in on this mild May day, with the young yellow-brown foliage of the oaks between me and the blue sky, the white star-flowers and the blue-eyed speedwell and the ground ivy at my feet, what grove of tropic palms, what strange ferns or splendid broad-petalled blossoms, could ever thrill such deep and delicate fibres within me as this home scene?

Text 2
My feelings seem to be those of our ancient earth in the daily ecstasy of its sun-kissed life; my own consciousness seems to stream through each blade of grass, each sucking root, to rise with the sap through the trees, to break out with joyous thrills in the waving fields of corn, in the rustling palm leaves.

Which choice best describes a notable difference in how the references to palm trees function in Text 1 and Text 2?

options.A: While the narrator of Text 1 and the author of Text 2 both refer to metaphorical palm trees, only the narrator of Text 1 suggests that the palm trees are representative of home.
options.B: While palm trees form part of a series conveying the variety of the natural world in both texts, only the author of Text 2 recognizes how closely interconnected palm trees are with other plants in their environment.
options.C: While the narrator of Text 1 and the author of Text 2 both discuss palm trees to suggest the value of experiencing the natural world, only the narrator of Text 1 alludes to the labor that goes into cultivating real palm trees.
options.D: While palm trees serve to evoke natural beauty in both texts, only the author of Text 2 expresses a close sense of identification with palm trees.

Bentley examined research on brown-throated three-toed sloths and canaries to see whether results from studies in the wild were consistent with the results of studies in the laboratory. Therefore, data showing that brown-throated three-toed sloths tend to sleep fewer than 10 hours per day in the wild would be irrelevant to Calisi-Rodriguez and Bentley's investigation if __________
